scope: Root's bookmark/collision lifetime integration, include and TrainerFrame ordering, and actual lifetime fixture. No production edits, no build, no game process or UI access.

checks.result: Bookmark acquisition pins the freshly observed generation before releasing the previous bookmark. Replacing the same bookmark balances the additional pin. Return requires actor/status/scene identity and both Resolve and ObserveCurrent equality before the native position call.

Collision acquisition pins once; retirement or completed/relinquished release unpins once. Unknown, off-current and observer-fault states retain the lease and block a replacement acquisition. Retirement is checked before any leased Actor dereference.

Pending restoration revalidates the current actor, exact generation, status/backlinks, scheduler and room. It clears only both owned bits with a null native override pointer; a partial foreign bit change or nonnull override relinquishes ownership without writing.

The role and lifetime helpers precede PlayerFeatures. ObserveCurrent and PlayerMaintainCollision run outside the fresh-host-only feature tick, so pending cleanup can complete while the host remains expired.

The fixture uses the production role helper, active actor list, status allocation pool and lifetime observer, replacing only native callbacks. Checks cover bookmark pin balance, same-address construction, pending off-current cleanup, foreign collision profile changes, host-expired frame cleanup, and observer-fault preservation. Final fatal-offcurrent regression also retains the lease/pin, calls real disabled OnFrame after the Actor returns, and verifies no future frame/cleanup work; fixture-only unwind is explicitly separated from product behavior.

testExecution.note: Final frozen source/test delta reviewed; 641/0 is Root-reported. No independent parallel build was performed.

limits: FatalFailure performs only a best-effort reset. If the original Actor is off-current or unverified, its collision lease remains unresolved; OnFrame returns immediately once g_disabled is set, so later recovery is not automatically serviced. A foreign-thread fatal failure skips the reset entirely. This is not evidence that the Actor was destroyed or that the effect was restored.

The final regression covers fatal failure while the Actor is off-current. Its pin and flags remain, returning to the Actor does not resume disabled OnFrame, and explicit fixture-only cleanup is not presented as a product recovery path.

The collision profile comparison cannot distinguish a later native writer that independently reasserts exactly the same two bits and null override pointer on the same Actor lifetime. This pre-existing value-ownership limit is separate from the now-guarded Actor-address ABA case.

Release during an unready or dead-but-still-allocated player phase intentionally does not require PlayerLiving: it requires a coherent current instance and performs only the two bounded masked clears. Unverifiable state is retained rather than guessed.

The observer's documented constructor coverage, foreign-thread/hook-loss fault handling, and bulk-teardown limits remain applicable. This narrow integration review does not re-prove all native observer bodies.
